g4ela-31-1-morphology: You learned a lot of word parts this year. Port means carry. Spect means look. Rupt means break. Pre means before. When you meet a long word, find a part you know, and the word starts to explain itself.
g4ela-31-2-grammar: Every punctuation mark has a job. A capital starts a sentence and a name. A comma joins or separates. Quotation marks hold someone’s exact words. Read your sentence out loud, and ask each mark: what’s your job?
g4ela-31-3-spelling: Before you hand in writing, check the patterns you know. Did a silent e drop before a suffix? Did a y change to i? Did a consonant double? Check one pattern at a time, and you’ll catch more.
g4ela-31-4-grammar: Your best sentence deserves a careful check. Capital at the start. Names capitalized. Commas where they join or separate. Quotation marks around exact words. An end mark that fits. Then read it out loud one last time.
